subject: Re: Deployment mode & data isolation — Dedicated vs Private VPC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Ross <samuel.ross@finsecure.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode recap & next steps — Redwood Inference

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: we discussed your primary requirement (data isolation for regulated customer PII and transaction logs) and three deployment options: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem.

Key notes from our conversation:
- FinSecure is leaning toward strict logical and network isolation; anything that shares a control plane with other tenants is risky for your auditors.
- Primary concerns: tenant isolation, KMS/CMK support (BYOK), audit log retention for 7 years, and the ability to prove no cross-tenant data leakage.
- Expected workload: ~200 concurrent inference sessions at peak, ~5M tokens/day, primarily inference (no training).
- Retention: transactional records stored for 7 years; ephemeral inference cache acceptable if flushed per request.

My read: Dedicated capacity gives you isolated GPU pools (no noisy neighbors on the runtime), but the control plane and management services are still hosted by Redwood; Private VPC (or on-prem) gives you a fully customer-controlled network and optional private control plane which matches compliance needs.

Attachments I can share right away: SOC2-Summary.pdf, high-level Private VPC datasheet, and a sample network diagram. I attached a short checklist below for the security team to confirm — after that we can schedule the security deep-dive and SE demo.

Security checklist (please fill):
1) Does FinSecure require customer-managed control plane (yes/no)?
2) Is BYOK/KMS required for inference keys and model encryption (yes/no)?
3) On-prem vs VPC: do you have an existing VPC peering/VPN requirement?
4) Expected RPS and sustained token throughput (numbers above OK?)
5) Compliance artifacts required (SOC2 report, penetration test results, architecture diagrams)

Next steps (proposed):
- You fill the checklist and send back any additional constraints.
- Tech deep-dive with Logan (SE) to go over network diagrams, KMS options, and PII handling — 60m.
- If Private VPC is required, schedule solution scoping (SOW, timeline, and pricing).

Available slots this week: Thu 4/30 10:00–11:30 PT, Fri 5/1 14:00–16:00 PT.

Thanks — look forward to your notes.

—

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Aisha (cc) is our lead on security/compliance and will weigh in on the checklist, but initial answers below:

1) Customer-managed control plane: Yes, preferred.
2) BYOK/KMS: Yes, we need BYOK for long-term storage and model keys.
3) VPC/On-prem: We prefer Private VPC (VPC in our account) over fully on-prem for now; we may consider on-prem later for higher-sensitivity workloads.
4) Throughput: The numbers you listed look right. Peak concurrency might be a little higher (250) during batch processing windows; plan for 300 to be safe.
5) Compliance artifacts: We will need SOC2 and penetration testing evidence, and a network diagram we can hand to our auditors.

A few specific questions:
- What does "private control plane" mean in practice? Is any metadata routed through Redwood-managed services?
- For Dedicated capacity: can we guarantee that other tenants never have access to the same runtime instance or disk volumes?
- What auditing/logging (WORM/immutable logs) options do you offer?
- Ballpark pricing and typical timelines for Private VPC onboarding?

If you can answer briefly, we can decide whether to move forward with a technical kickoff.

Thanks,

Thanks Sam — great questions. Short answers below, attaching the SOC2 summary and Private VPC datasheet for your auditors.

1) "Private control plane" — In our Private VPC offering the control plane (management API, auth, and telemetry) can be deployed into your VPC or connected via a customer-controlled VPN/PrivateLink. That means metadata (request IDs, metrics) does not traverse public Redwood-managed networks. There are two flavors: (a) customer-managed control plane in your VPC (preferred for strict compliance), or (b) host-managed control plane with strict isolation and contractual guarantees. We can scope both in the SOW.

2) Dedicated capacity isolation — Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools and dedicated disk for model artifacts and caches. Runtime instances are single-tenant (no other customers scheduled on your nodes) but the control plane remains hosted unless you choose the Private control plane option. We use encrypted disk and per-tenant keying for dedicated workloads; we can provide attestation for instance isolation.

3) Auditing/logging — We support forwarding immutable audit logs to customer-managed Cloud Storage (S3/GCS) and to SIEMs via secure connectors. Logs can be WORM/immutable based on your storage provider policies; Redwood can configure retention and export rules.

4) BYOK/KMS — Supported for both Private VPC and Dedicated; for Private VPC you keep full key control (BYOK) and we never have access to key material. For Dedicated we support customer KMS integration for model/artifact encryption and request-level encryption.

5) Timeline & pricing (ballpark) —
- Private VPC: 6–10 weeks typical (scoping, network work, security review), depending on procurement and audit windows.
- Dedicated: 2–4 weeks for reserved capacity setup but with hosted control plane; shorter technical onboarding.
- Pricing: I can share a preliminary range in the tech call; fine-grained pricing depends on committed GPU hours and support SLA.

Next steps: Logan can run the technical deep-dive to validate network diagram and KMS options. Can we aim for Fri 5/1 14:00 PT (you already suggested) for a 60m SE call? If that works I will send a calendar invite and share the network diagram and a short checklist for the SE.

Attaching: SOC2-Summary.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-data-sheet.pdf, network-diagram-vpc.png

—
Marissa
